note: Blind test of on-the-fly ratio screening. NO hints about tool/param names — discover from schema. Judge whether the RESULT actually matches the user's intent.

cases.question: Find companies that spend between 10% and 20% of their revenue on R&D.
cases.acceptance: Returns a non-empty list where each result's R&D is roughly 10-20% of revenue (a two-sided ratio band of two line items). NOT a single-metric threshold.

cases.question: Which companies have capital expenditure of around 8% of revenue?
cases.acceptance: Returns companies whose capex/revenue sits near 8% (capital-intensive names like energy/utilities/telecom are plausible). Capex is an outflow — magnitude, not sign, is what matters.

cases.question: Find companies whose R&D is at least 15% of their revenue.
cases.acceptance: Returns R&D-heavy companies where R&D/revenue >= 0.15 (a one-sided fraction-of relation). Non-empty, plausible (software/biotech/semis).

cases.question: Show me companies where free cash flow covers the dividend at least twice over.
cases.acceptance: Returns dividend payers whose FCF >= 2x dividends paid (a coverage relation). Non-empty and plausible.

cases.question: Find companies with a net profit margin above 20%.
cases.acceptance: A plain single-metric level screen (net_margin > 0.20). Non-empty. This is a CONTROL — it must still work normally.
